reason: The cited evidence confirms that the studied HEAs are BCS superconductors (E1, E3) and mentions that electron count can impact superconductivity (E2), but none of the passages provides specific data or analysis demonstrating that VEC governs Tc through N(EF) in HEAs outside Nb–Ta systems, nor that increasing VEC shifts the Fermi level to enhance N(EF) and coupling. The key mechanistic premises thus lack direct evidential support.
premises: Tc is governed primarily by valence electron count (VEC) via its effect on the density of states at the Fermi level N(EF)
Increasing VEC shifts the Fermi level into regions of enhanced N(EF)
Enhanced N(EF) strengthens electron–phonon coupling and modulates Tc
The cited HEAs are BCS-type superconductors where N(EF) and electron–phonon coupling determine Tc
VEC variations explain Tc differences in HEAs outside Nb–Ta systems
